title: TypeScript Basics
summary: Add types to your values so mistakes are caught before the app runs.
heading: TypeScript Basics

blocks.text: Plain JavaScript lets you put anything in any variable, so a typo or wrong value only blows up when the app runs. TypeScript lets you say what kind of value belongs where, and warns you while you type — long before a user ever sees it.
Add a type after a colon. These are the everyday ones you'll use constantly.

blocks.label: types

blocks.text: You don't always have to write the type. If you give a value right away, TypeScript figures the type out for you — and still protects it.

blocks.label: inference
blocks.code:
let city = "Delhi"; // inferred as string

city = 42; // Error: a number isn't a string

blocks.text: Let TypeScript infer when it's obvious; add a type yourself when it makes the code clearer.
any turns the safety off for a value — avoid it. unknown is the safe version: you must check what it is before using it.

blocks.label: any vs unknown

blocks.text: Reaching for any a lot usually means you're fighting the types. Prefer real types or unknown.

items: TypeScript checks types before the code runs.
Inference fills in obvious types for you.
